---
title: "BCOS: transport with killing and competing risks"
---

This appendix develops a model of deterministic transport with interior killing and boundary absorption, and describes its application to BCOS in PRESS. The forward equation for diffusion with killing and absorption studied by Holcman, Marchewka and Schuss [@holcman2005] motivates the mathematical structure. Here, deterministic transport is combined with a probabilistic reference law and competing terminal events.

## 1. Reference transport model {#reference-transport-model}

Consider a particle moving along a one-dimensional domain $(0,L)$, with absorption at $L$. Conditional on its initial position or boundary entry, its motion in the domain is deterministic until killing or absorption. Let $L>0$ and let $\tau:[0,L]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, strictly increasing and $C^1$ on $(0,L]$, with $\tau'(\ell)>0$. Define

$$
\nu(\ell)=\frac{1}{\tau'(\ell)},\qquad \dot X_t=\nu(X_t),\quad \ell>0.
$$

For $\kappa>0$, introduce the logistic reference function

$$
F(\ell,t)=\left[1+\exp\{-\kappa\,[t-\tau(\ell)]\}\right]^{-1}.
$$

Its spatial density and current are

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_0(\ell,t)&=-\partial_\ell F(\ell,t)=\kappa\,\tau'(\ell)F(\ell,t)[1-F(\ell,t)],\\
 \nu(\ell)p_0(\ell,t)&=\partial_tF(\ell,t)=\kappa F(\ell,t)[1-F(\ell,t)].
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p_0=-\partial_\ell F$ and $\nu p_0=\partial_tF$, equality of the mixed derivatives gives

$$
\partial_tp_0+\partial_\ell(\nu p_0)=0.
$$

## 2. Initial conditioning and boundary inflow {#initial-conditioning-and-boundary-inflow}

At $t=0$, the reference probability is partitioned into a left reservoir of mass $1-F(0,0)$, an interior mass $F(0,0)-F(L,0)$, and a right component of mass $F(L,0)$. The reservoir is a scalar state that represents probability not yet entered into the transport domain. No killing occurs in this state. We remove only the right component and condition on non-absorption at time zero. Set

$$
\boxed{Z=1-F(L,0)>0.}
$$

The initial interior density and reservoir mass are

$$
p_k(\ell,0)=\frac{p_0(\ell,0)}{Z},\quad 0<\ell<L,\qquad M_{\mathrm{res}}(0)=\frac{1-F(0,0)}{Z}.
$$

By integration of $-\partial_\ell F$,

$$
M_{\mathrm{res}}(0)+\int_0^L p_0(\ell,0)/Z\,\mathrm{d} \ell=\frac{1-F(0,0)+F(0,0)-F(L,0)}{Z}=1.
$$

The conditioned reference inflow is

$$
j_{\mathrm{in}}(t)=\frac{\partial_tF(0,t)}{Z},\qquad M_{\mathrm{res}}'(t)=-j_{\mathrm{in}}(t).
$$

Integrating with the initial reservoir mass yields

$$
\boxed{M_{\mathrm{res}}(t)=\frac{1-F(0,t)}{Z}.}
$$

Thus $M_{\mathrm{res}}(t)\ge0$, $M_{\mathrm{res}}(t)\to0$, and $\int_0^\infty j_{\mathrm{in}}(t)\,\mathrm{d} t=M_{\mathrm{res}}(0)$.

The inflow is driven by the boundary logistic $F(0,t)$, centred at $\tau(0)$. For any $0<\epsilon<L$, the conditioned initial probability of being beyond $\epsilon$ in the domain is

$$
\Pr(X_0>\epsilon\mid\text{not absorbed})=\frac{F(\epsilon,0)-F(L,0)}{Z}.
$$

If $\tau(0)\ge0$, strict monotonicity implies $\tau(\epsilon)>0$, so this probability tends to zero as $\kappa\to\infty$. The initial law therefore concentrates at the origin, with the reservoir interpreted as mass waiting to enter. When $\tau(0)=0$, the unconditioned boundary logistic has $F(0,0)=1/2$; retaining the reservoir preserves this uncertainty without requiring a spatial extension to negative positions.

## 3. Transport with killing {#transport-with-killing}

Let $k(\ell,t)\ge0$ be a killing intensity on $(0,L)$. Assume that $k$ is measurable and bounded on $[0,L]$ over each finite time interval (boundary values may be assigned arbitrarily). This sufficient condition ensures finite characteristic integrals and the flux balances below. Boundary currents are understood as traces, almost everywhere in time when necessary. The defective density $p_k$ satisfies

$$
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
 \partial_tp_k+\partial_\ell(\nu p_k)&=-kp_k, &&0<\ell<L,\\
 p_k(\ell,0)&=p_0(\ell,0)/Z,\\
 \lim_{\ell\downarrow0}\nu(\ell)p_k(\ell,t)&=j_{\mathrm{in}}(t), &&t>0.
 \end{aligned}}
$$

No density boundary condition is imposed at the outflow boundary $L$. The left condition is stated on the current. The initial current is compatible with the boundary data:

$$
\lim_{\ell\downarrow0}\nu(\ell)p_k(\ell,0)=\frac{\partial_tF(0,0)}{Z}=j_{\mathrm{in}}(0).
$$

## 4. Solution by characteristics {#solution-by-characteristics}

For a characteristic ending at $(\ell,t)$,

$$
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm d\xi}\tau(X_\xi)=\tau'(X_\xi)\nu(X_\xi)=1,
\qquad X_\xi=\tau^{-1}(\tau(\ell)-t+\xi).
$$

The backward characteristic reaches either the initial line at $\xi=0$ or the inflow boundary at $\xi=t-\tau(\ell)+\tau(0)$. Both cases are represented by

$$
\xi_*(\ell,t)=\max\{0,t-\tau(\ell)+\tau(0)\}.
$$

The inverse of $\tau$ is evaluated only on its range over $[0,L]$. If $t<\tau(\ell)-\tau(0)$, the characteristic starts inside the domain at $X_0>0$; otherwise it enters at $X_{\xi_*}=0$.

Write $J_k=\nu p_k$. To derive the characteristic equation without differentiating $\nu$, change to the transport-time coordinate $\zeta=\tau(\ell)-\tau(0)$. Since $\mathrm d\ell=\nu(\ell)\,\mathrm d\zeta$, the density in this coordinate is $J_k$, expressed as a function of $(\zeta,t)$. The conservative equation becomes

$$
\partial_t J_k+\partial_\zeta J_k=-kJ_k,
$$

where $k$ is evaluated at $\ell=\tau^{-1}(\zeta+\tau(0))$. Along a characteristic,

$$
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm d\xi}J_k(X_\xi,\xi)=-k(X_\xi,\xi)J_k(X_\xi,\xi).
$$

Integration gives

$$
J_k(\ell,t)=J_k(X_{\xi_*},\xi_*)\exp\!\left[-\int_{\xi_*}^t k(X_\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm d\xi\right].
$$

The reference function $F$ is constant along each characteristic because $\xi-\tau(X_\xi)=t-\tau(\ell)$. Its reference current $\partial_tF=\kappa F(1-F)$ is therefore also constant. Both the initial current and the inflow current are equal to the corresponding reference current divided by $Z$. Hence

$$
J_k(X_{\xi_*},\xi_*)=\frac{\partial_tF(\ell,t)}{Z}.
$$

Dividing by $\nu(\ell)$ yields the solution

$$
\boxed{p_k(\ell,t)=\frac{p_0(\ell,t)}{Z}w(\ell,t),\qquad
w(\ell,t)=\exp\!\left[-\int_{\xi_*}^t k(X_\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm d\xi\right].}
$$

The weight $w$ is the probability of surviving killing along the characteristic segment inside the domain. The inflow preserves the reference density on characteristics originating at the boundary. For finite integrated killing, the density is positive throughout the interior at finite times. Without killing, $p_k=p_0/Z$.

The solution satisfies the inflow condition of the problem. For fixed $t>0$ and sufficiently small $\ell>0$, $\xi_*=t-\tau(\ell)+\tau(0)$. By continuity of $\tau$ at zero, $t-\xi_*=\tau(\ell)-\tau(0)\to0$. If $K$ bounds the killing intensity over the relevant finite time interval,

$$
0\le\int_{\xi_*}^t k(X_\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm{d}\xi\le K[\tau(\ell)-\tau(0)]\longrightarrow0.
$$

Thus $w(\ell,t)\to1$ and, using the reference current identity,

$$
\lim_{\ell\downarrow0}J_k(\ell,t)
 =\lim_{\ell\downarrow0}\frac{\partial_t F(\ell,t)}{Z}w(\ell,t)
 =\frac{\partial_t F(0,t)}{Z}=j_{\mathrm{in}}(t).
$$

At $t=0$ the weight is identically one, so the initial and boundary currents also agree at the corner.

## 5. Competing risks {#competing-risks}

The terminal fluxes are

$$
\boxed{j_L(t)=\nu(L)p_k(L^-,t),\qquad j_k(t)=\int_0^L k(\ell,t)p_k(\ell,t)\,\mathrm{d} \ell.}
$$

Integration of the transport equation over $(0,L)$ gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\int_0^L p_k(\ell,t)\,\mathrm d\ell=j_{\mathrm{in}}(t)-j_L(t)-j_k(t).
$$

The total at-risk probability includes the reservoir:

$$
\boxed{S(t)=M_{\mathrm{res}}(t)+\int_0^L p_k(\ell,t)\,\mathrm d\ell.}
$$

Since $M_{\mathrm{res}}'=-j_{\mathrm{in}}$, the inflow cancels from the total balance. With $C_L$ and $C_k$ denoting cumulative incidences of absorption and of killing, respectively,

$$
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
 S'&=-j_L-j_k, & S(0)&=1,\\
 C_L'&=j_L, & C_L(0)&=0,\\
 C_k'&=j_k, & C_k(0)&=0.
 \end{aligned}}
$$

Adding the equations yields $S(t)+C_L(t)+C_k(t)=1$. These balances hold almost everywhere in time under the stated integrability assumptions.

For $S(t)>0$, the cause-specific hazards are

$$
\boxed{h_L(t)=\frac{j_L(t)}{S(t)},\qquad h_k(t)=\frac{j_k(t)}{S(t)}.}
$$

The total hazard is $h_L+h_k=-S'/S$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
S(t)&=\exp\!\left[-\int_0^t [h_L(\xi)+h_k(\xi)]\,\mathrm{d}\xi\right],\\
 C_L(t)&=\int_0^t h_L(\xi)S(\xi)\,\mathrm{d}\xi,\qquad C_k(t)=\int_0^t h_k(\xi)S(\xi)\,\mathrm{d}\xi.
\end{aligned}
$$

The reservoir contributes to the denominator but not to either terminal flux. Since $M_{\mathrm{res}}(t)>0$ at every finite time, $S(t)>0$.

### Multiple killing causes

Suppose killing can occur through several competing causes indexed by $i$, with local intensities $k_i(\ell,t)$. Conditional on the particle's trajectory, assume independent killing processes, so that

$$
k(\ell,t)=\sum_i k_i(\ell,t).
$$

Along a characteristic, the survival weight factorizes as

$$
w(\ell,t)=\prod_{i}\exp\!\left[-\int_{\xi_*}^t k_i(X_\xi,\xi)\,\mathrm d\xi\right].
$$

The additive sink partitions the interception flux into mutually exclusive terminal causes:

$$
j_i(t)=\int_0^L k_i(\ell,t)p_k(\ell,t)\,\mathrm{d}\ell,\qquad
j_k(t)=\sum_i j_i(t).
$$

The cause-specific hazards and cumulative incidences are

$$
h_i(t)=\frac{j_i(t)}{S(t)},\qquad C_i(t)=\int_0^t S(\xi)h_i(\xi)\,\mathrm{d}\xi.
$$

Consequently $S(t)+C_L(t)+\sum_i C_i(t)=1$. The individual fluxes depend on all killing intensities through the surviving density $p_k$.

## 6. Terminal probabilities {#terminal-probabilities}

Since $0\le w\le1$, we have $0\le S(t)\le [1-F(L,t)]/Z\to0$. Consequently, the terminal probabilities satisfy

$$
C_L(\infty)=\int_0^\infty j_L(t)\,\mathrm{d} t,\qquad C_k(\infty)=\int_0^\infty j_k(t)\,\mathrm{d} t,\qquad C_L(\infty)+C_k(\infty)=1.
$$

Substituting the characteristic solution into the boundary current gives

$$
C_L(\infty)=\frac1Z\int_0^\infty \partial_tF(L,t)w(L,t)\,\mathrm{d}t.
$$

If $k(\ell,t)=k(\ell)$, the change of variable $\eta=X_\xi$ gives $\,\mathrm{d} \xi=\,\mathrm{d} \eta/\nu(\eta)$. The survival weight is $\exp[-\int_y^\ell k(\eta)/\nu(\eta)\,\mathrm{d} \eta]$ for initial-line characteristics and $\exp[-\int_0^\ell k(\eta)/\nu(\eta)\,\mathrm{d} \eta]$ for boundary characteristics. The final probability is therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
C_L(\infty)={}&\int_0^L p_0(y,0)/Z\exp\!\left[-\int_y^L\frac{k(\eta)}{\nu(\eta)}\,\mathrm{d} \eta\right]\,\mathrm{d} y\\
 &+M_{\mathrm{res}}(0)\exp\!\left[-\int_0^L\frac{k(\eta)}{\nu(\eta)}\,\mathrm{d} \eta\right].
\end{aligned}
$$

The two terms correspond to the initial interior mass and the initial reservoir, respectively.

Without killing, $w=1$ and $j_L(t)=\partial_tF(L,t)/Z$, so $C_L(\infty)=[1-F(L,0)]/Z=1$.

For multiple killing causes, $C_L(\infty)+\sum_i C_i(\infty)=1$.

## 7. Application to BCOS in PRESS {#application-to-bcos-in-press}

### Time to intercept and reference law

The function $\tau(\ell)$ of the transport model is the time to intercept (TTI) of the carrier along the candidate route, and the killing is the interception of the carrier by the defenders. For a player $j$ and a target location $x$ on the pitch, the nominal TTI is

$$
\tau_j(x)=t_{\mathrm{turn},j}(x)+t_{\mathrm{move},j}(x),
$$

the sum of the turning delay and the acceleration-limited travel time, both computed from the observed position and velocity of the player. The maximal speed and acceleration of the movement model are set separately for the carrier, who moves with the ball, and for the defenders. For a defender, $\tau_j(x)$ is the nominal time to reach a potential interception location; for the carrier, it is the nominal time to reach $x$. Following Spearman [@spearman2017; @spearman2018beyond], the uncertainty around the TTI is logistic, with arrival-time distribution and arrival hazard

$$
F_j(x,t)=\left[1+\exp\{-\kappa\,[t-\tau_j(x)]\}\right]^{-1},\qquad
\lambda_j^{\mathrm{arr}}(t\mid x)=\frac{\partial_tF_j(x,t)}{1-F_j(x,t)}=\kappa F_j(x,t).
$$

Here $\kappa=\pi/(\sqrt{3}\,s)$, where $s$ is the standard deviation of arrival-time uncertainty.

For a carrier initially at $x_{\mathrm{bc}}(0)$, the route is $x(\ell;z)=x_{\mathrm{bc}}(0)+\ell(z-x_{\mathrm{bc}}(0))/L$, with $L=\|z-x_{\mathrm{bc}}(0)\|$. Along this route, $\tau(\ell)$ is the nominal TTI of the carrier at $x(\ell;z)$, and $F(\ell,t)$ is its logistic arrival-time distribution. The killing intensity is the arrival hazard of the defenders at the carrier's location, as specified below. 

### Transport velocity

The TTI of the carrier along a straight ray follows from the acceleration-limited movement model of PRESS. Let $\ell$ denote distance along a straight ray from the carrier's initial position. The observed speed is $u\ge0$, and $a>0$ and $v_{\max}>0$ are the carrier's acceleration and maximal speed. The angle $\theta$ is fixed along the ray. The turning contribution is the constant

$$
t_{\mathrm{turn}}=\frac{u\theta}{a_{\mathrm{turn}}},\qquad a_{\mathrm{turn}}>0.
$$

For $u<v_{\max}$, set

$$
t_a=\frac{v_{\max}-u}{a},\qquad d_a=ut_a+\tfrac12at_a^2.
$$

The function defining the transport is

$$
\tau(\ell)=t_{\mathrm{turn}}+\begin{cases}
 (\sqrt{u^2+2a\ell}-u)/a,&0\le \ell\le d_a,\\[3pt]
 t_a+(\ell-d_a)/v_{\max},&\ell>d_a.
 \end{cases}
$$

For $u\ge v_{\max}$, use $\tau(\ell)=t_{\mathrm{turn}}+\ell/u$: the observed speed is maintained, including when it exceeds $v_{\max}$. For the accelerating case,

$$
\tau'(\ell)=\begin{cases}
 1/\sqrt{u^2+2a\ell},&0<\ell\le d_a,\\
 1/v_{\max},&\ell>d_a,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \nu(\ell)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{u^2+2a\ell},&0<\ell\le d_a,\\
 v_{\max},&\ell>d_a.
 \end{cases}
$$

At $d_a$, $u^2+2ad_a=v_{\max}^2$, so $\tau$ is $C^1$.

The inverse in the accelerating case is

$$
\tau^{-1}(t)=\begin{cases}
 u(t-t_{\mathrm{turn}})+\tfrac12a(t-t_{\mathrm{turn}})^2,&0\le t-t_{\mathrm{turn}}\le t_a,\\
 d_a+v_{\max}(t-t_{\mathrm{turn}}-t_a),&t-t_{\mathrm{turn}}>t_a.
 \end{cases}
$$

For $u\ge v_{\max}$, the inverse is $\tau^{-1}(t)=u(t-t_{\mathrm{turn}})$. These expressions can be substituted directly into the characteristic solution. The constant $t_{\mathrm{turn}}$ cancels from $\nu$, $\xi_*$ and the characteristic trajectories, but affects the logistic reference weights and initial conditioning.

Since $\tau(0)=t_{\mathrm{turn}}\ge0$, the initial concentration result applies.

### Interception intensities

Interception occurs when a defender reaches the location occupied by the carrier while the carrier is still in possession. In pitch control, the arrival of each player is evaluated at every point of the ball trajectory, and each point represents an opportunity for interception. Here the arrival of each defender is evaluated in the same way at every point of the carrier's route, and we model the local interception intensity by the defender’s arrival hazard at that location. Conditional on the carrier’s characteristic and the observed tracking state, the defenders’ interception processes are assumed independent; their intensities therefore add. This neglects explicit interactions between defenders. For the route $x(\ell;z)$, PRESS specifies the local killing intensity as

$$
k(\ell,t)=\sum_{i\in\mathrm{opp}} k_i(\ell,t),\qquad
k_i(\ell,t)=\lambda_i^{\mathrm{arr}}\big(t\mid x(\ell;z)\big)=\kappa F_i(x(\ell;z),t).
$$

For a finite number of defenders, $0\le k\le n_{\mathrm{opp}}\kappa$, satisfying the boundedness assumption above.

### Accessibility and defender-specific risks

The accessibility probability is $p_{\mathrm{bc}}(z)=C_L(\infty)$. The terminal incidence $C_i(\infty)$ is the probability that defender $i$ causes the first interception. Hence

$$
p_{\mathrm{bc}}(z)+\sum_{i\in\mathrm{opp}} C_i(\infty)=1.
$$

These incidences quantify the contributions of individual defenders under the joint model. Evaluating $p_{\mathrm{bc}}(z)$ across candidate destinations produces the BCOS accessibility surface.
